reviews.title: unavailable, despite update
reviews.text: I updated my NYT cooking app three days ago. Despite the update, I am blocked by a notice to update the app before it will be possible to get onto the page. Very frustrating, as the recipes are great.

reviews.title: Locked out by New Version
reviews.text: My trusty iPad doesn’t support iOS 18 so I now find myself locked out of the recipe collection I had stored. Why does the NYT think we should all rush out and buy new Apple devices suddenly? Support for older technology is green and caring for the environment. Farewell and thanks for all the fish.

reviews.title: Forced updates
reviews.text: Please don’t force us to update the 120MB app when we’re trying to cook our family a meal.

reviews.title: Added AI garbage
reviews.text: This app used to be fantastic, the only thing I’d give NYT my money for. Then they forced AI garbage upon us and left no ability to turn it off.

reviews.title: Just because you can doesn’t mean you should
reviews.text:
Why the AI? Why is it all up in my face when I open the app? I’m afraid I’m going to accidentally click on it. It is completely unnecessary. If you feel like you have to have it, fine. Make it optional. I don’t want to see it. Even better, make it optional and make it an opt-in prompt, not opt out. 

Generally, I like this recipe app for inspiration and community feedback. But AI leaves a bad taste in my mouth, which doesn’t really help when you’re trying to cook.

reviews.title: Ads when you have a subscription?
reviews.text: App itself is good but why am I seeing an ad every third scroll down that’s the entire screen???

reviews.title: Computer write me a recipe make no mistakes
reviews.text: Isn’t the value of paying for a New York Times cooking subscription the access to a collection of human knowledge and expertise? Oh well…

reviews.title: Will not save recipes
reviews.text: I find old saved recipes but cannot seem to save any new ones. Some sort of glitch or it’s just wonky app. Should allow us to access this on regular NYT app.

reviews.title: Why add AI???
reviews.text: AI features were added so you can enjoy slop in your recipes. Plus you can’t disable the feature! Why even add this?

reviews.title: Impossible to opt-out of AI integration
reviews.text: No thanks

reviews.title: Making your app worse to push ai
reviews.text: Why would I pay for this? If I wanted to use AI in concert with your recipes, I could already do that. Not gaining anything by adding it to your app, just making it worse

reviews.title: Ugh enough with the AI
reviews.text: This was of the few wholesome corners of my library of digital tools that, had not been overrun with sycophantic AI drivel. Until now. I’ll reluctantly tolerate the bots pestering me in Excel but not while I’m using something that’s supposed to bring me joy. Something about adding an AI feature to this particular app just makes me sad. The whole point was the recipes and comments written in real voices. I plan to download the recipes I like and move on.  💔

reviews.title: Used to love it
reviews.text: Used this app all the time but new version won’t run on my iPad anymore. Please allow versioning. And really did you need to add ai to something that already worked fantastically?

reviews.title: WTF AI
reviews.text: WAS a great app, idk what this AI nonsense is to have it as part of the recipe functions now? I prefer saving the planet for our children & wildlife. And I can’t even opt out of it while subscription prices go up to pay for the AI no one asked for. I DON’T NEED AI TO BE INVOLVED IN MY COOKING

reviews.title: New ai features are bad
reviews.text: The ai features tank this app

reviews.title: Let me turn off AI
reviews.text: I have loved this app. For many years. I also thought the NYT had some of a moral compass left and a taste for class, but it seems they have given us what nobody asked for, an AI addition to the app and no way to turn it off. Please NYT, allow users to turn off AI chat. Let cooking stay human.

reviews.title: Can’t turn AI off
reviews.text: Now has annoying AI prompt that you can’t turn off. I don’t want to see AI on absolutely everything I use!

reviews.title: AI cannot be disabled
reviews.text: Bought a subscription to avoid AI junk. Now there is an AI bot box that is highlighted in red and cycles through text while you are trying to read the recipe ingredients. Incredibly disappointing and annoying.

reviews.title: Unwanted AI
reviews.text:
Used to love this app. I have since deleted it due to the new update that doesn’t make AI option. 

Do better, NYT.

reviews.title: Need access to older version no longer compatible with my only 1 yo os
reviews.text: Please allow versioning.

reviews.title: No one asked for AI (the recipe customization tool)
reviews.text:
I do not want AI involved in this app at all and will no longer be using it as long as there are such options.

I can't think of a more specifically human experience (maybe sex?) than the act of cooking and eating. I love reading what other readers thought and what their little hacks are. Having AI be involved in this is extremely sad.

reviews.title: Ruined the share sheet
reviews.text: Share sheet is buggy and they now seem to have blocked the app from showing shortcuts or even an open in browsers button.

reviews.title: Text size not adjustable
reviews.text: I love NYT, but I’m disappointed that the cooking app does not allow for larger text size. No adjustment option in the app and it does not support larger text size when chosen in phone settings. You have a lot of older readers who need larger text. Please fix this.

reviews.title: i don't need to chat with a recipe bot
reviews.text: i've been using this app nearly every day since it came out but i might get rid of it over the new AI nonsense. nobody wants this

reviews.title: Used to be a 5-star app, but now infected with AI
reviews.text:
I love this app. I use it almost daily. I love scrolling it like it’s some foodie social media. The subscription is worth the price for me. 

But alas, like the rest of our planet, the NYT Cooking app has become infected with AI. My immediate thought was, there goes the quality… It seems like no matter how unnecessary it is, AI really is coming to destroy every last thing we love. Sad day.

reviews.title: AI feature is dumb
reviews.text: Why are you jamming AI into this app? Wholly unnecessary and distracting from the recipes…won’t be subscribing again when mine runs out, disappointing.

reviews.title: Went downhill
reviews.text: I used to love spending time looking at recipes and reading reviews by real people, but now the NYT thought we needed AI to customize recipes and those chats are used to train AI per their TOS. I do not want any part of that.

reviews.title: Now with AI?
reviews.text: I was considering buying a subscription, but count me out with this new AI feature. Not willing to put my dollars toward a feature no one asked for.

reviews.title: Why ai??
reviews.text: I loved this app until they introduced ai! I wish there was a way to opt out. I will not be renewing.

reviews.title: Adored this app…until they introduced AI
reviews.text: use the NYT Cooking app weekly to try new recipes. I choose to pay for it because I value recipes tested by people, the chance to work with my hands, and a reliable resource amid so much AI-generated content. I’m disappointed to see NYT Cooking shoehorning AI into the app. Human expertise is a big part of what makes it worth paying for, and I hope you reconsider this direction.

reviews.title: Can’t opt-out of AI
reviews.text: I don’t want AI in my cooking app. AI doesn’t eat. There should be an option to not have it in the app. Why does a cooking app need AI?? Food is a human experience!

reviews.title: AI is dumb
reviews.text:
I have always loved NYT Cooking and subscribe to the Times primarily because of it.

But now I might delete the app. The Times has introduced an AI feature that will ruin their recipes, just you watch. 

Recipes are meant to be written and tested by humans. An AI agent cannot taste, touch, smell or see. We’re cutting down forests, wasting water, emitting pollutants and creating unbearable noise pollution for what?! I see no value added — and much lost — with the introduction of AI into the NYT Cooking app. 

I wonder how the staff who develop recipes will feel about this change and whether they too will consider walking away rather than see their work bowdlerized.

reviews.title: More AI BS
reviews.text: Not the NYT wedging unwanted AI features into everything now. I want recipes tested and created by people NOT LLMs. Nobody wants these features. I will be canceling my subscription.

reviews.title: Being ruined by AI
reviews.text: Way to ruin a previously great recipe app by forcing AI into it, NYT. Cooking is one of the basic human pleasures. AI has no place in the kitchen.

reviews.title: No AI
reviews.text: Remove the AI

reviews.title: Awful AI inclusion
reviews.text: I’ve had NYT cooking for multiple years and love everything about it- that was until they started forcing an AI agent on me in the app. Why on earth would I want AI to write the recipes when the whole reason I use NYT Cooking is for the amazing chefs and writers? Cancelled my membership, only using my cookbooks now.

reviews.title: No one wants AI
reviews.text: Completely unnecessary to add generative AI. No one asked for this or wants bland, generic, unchecked recipes by robots. The whole point is people-tested and created recipes then input from other humans in comments.

reviews.title: Get the AI recipe agent out of here
reviews.text: No one wants this. Defeats the whole point. Please remove

reviews.title: No AI
reviews.text: Really really bummed that an AI feature was added to the app

reviews.title: AI is an unnecessary distraction
reviews.text: I use this app frequently but to see AI now integrated is frustrating and completely unnecessary. It’s a complete waste of resources and takes away from the very basics of critical thinking.

reviews.title: AI Being Implemented
reviews.text: As a years long daily user of this app, I can say this is an awful change. Who on earth thought adding AI to a cooking app was a good idea? They should be fired. Full stop.

reviews.title: WTAF?
reviews.text:
Since the “upgrade”, the app will no longer work on my iPad 6g. Who decided to make the new design not backward compatible?

It’s hard for me to read a recipe off of the phone while I’m cooking, and any “new” features (which I have yet to notice) don’t justify ruining the app on older devices.

reviews.title: App crashing
reviews.text: App offline a lot of the time which is making it unusable. Shame because some recipes are good.

reviews.title: Focus on Food
reviews.text:
The original app was focused on food. It is now riddled with advertisements that distract to the extent I give up using the app. 
Food focus should be the only thing.
What a shame and I’ve been a NYT subscriber for years.

reviews.title: Ads on a paid subscription.
reviews.text: They seriously started showing ads on a paid for subscription. Wild.

reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.text: I cant believe that im paying for this app and cant open it if I dont have ios18

reviews.text:
Tells me to DL the latest compatible version…
Which doesn’t work either😬
Catch 22

What to do?…

reviews.title: Excluded!
reviews.text: Now the app requires iOS 18+ I can no longer access it on my older iPad. Unless that changes, I will have to unsubscribe. Shame as it’s a great app.

reviews.title: Update means I can no longer access.
reviews.text: I’ve been a subscriber of NYT for many years but today I had to cancel my subscription because this update means I can no longer access the Cooking part of my subscription. Thanks a million. NYT!!
